name: Sandworm Team – APT Threat Map
description: Técnicas de Sandworm Team com cobertura do catálogo (score 3=regra, 2=parcial, 1=lacuna)

techniques.comment: Sandworm Team has used its plainpwd tool, a modified version of Mimikatz, and comsvcs.dll to dump Windows credentials from system memory. | cobertura: regra
Sandworm Team has used `ntdsutil.exe` to back up the Active Directory database, likely for credential access. | cobertura: regra
Sandworm Team has exfiltrated internal documents, files, and other data from compromised hosts. | cobertura: regra
Sandworm Team has used a tool to query Active Directory using LDAP, discovering information about computers listed in AD. | cobertura: regra
Sandworm Team has copied payloads to the `ADMIN$` share of remote systems and run `net use` to connect to network shares. | cobertura: regra
Sandworm Team has used Base64 encoding within malware variants. | cobertura: regra
Sandworm Team has used ROT13 encoding, AES encryption and compression with the zlib library for their Python-based backdoor. | cobertura: regra
Sandworm Team has collected the username from a compromised host. | cobertura: regra
Sandworm Team masqueraded malicious installers as Windows update packages to evade defense and entice users to execute binaries. | cobertura: regra
Sandworm Team has avoided detection by naming a malicious binary explorer.exe. | cobertura: regra
Sandworm Team has used intercepter-NG to sniff passwords in network traffic. | cobertura: regra
Sandworm Team has sent system information to its C2 server using HTTP. | cobertura: regra
Sandworm Team has used Impacket’s WMIexec module for remote code execution and VBScript to run WMI queries. | cobertura: regra

Sandworm Team had gathered user, IP address, and server data related to RDP sessions on a compromised host. It has also accessed network diagram files useful for understanding how a host's network was configured. | cobertura: regra
Sandworm Team leveraged SHARPIVORY, a .NET dropper that writes embedded payload to disk and uses scheduled tasks to persist on victim machines. | cobertura: regra
Sandworm Team has used a keylogger to capture keystrokes by using the SetWindowsHookEx function. | cobertura: regra
Sandworm Team has used PowerShell scripts to run a credential harvesting tool in memory to evade defenses. | cobertura: regra
Sandworm Team has created VBScripts to run an SSH server. | cobertura: regra
Sandworm Team has used backdoors that can delete files used in an attack from an infected system. | cobertura: regra
Sandworm Team's BCS-server tool connects to the designated C2 server via HTTP. | cobertura: regra
Sandworm Team has used the commercially available tool RemoteExec for agentless remote code execution. | cobertura: regra
Sandworm Team have used previously acquired legitimate credentials prior to attacks. | cobertura: regra
Sandworm Team has used stolen credentials to access administrative accounts within the domain. | cobertura: regra
Sandworm Team used a backdoor to enumerate information about the infected system's operating system. | cobertura: regra
Sandworm Team has enumerated files on a compromised host. | cobertura: regra
Sandworm Team has used a tool to query Active Directory using LDAP, discovering information about usernames listed in AD. | cobertura: regra
Sandworm Team used malware to enumerate email settings, including usernames and passwords, from the M.E.Doc application. | cobertura: regra

Sandworm Team's BCS-server tool can create an internal proxy server to redirect traffic from the adversary-controlled C2 to internal servers which may not be connected to the internet, but are interconnected locally. | cobertura: regra

Sandworm Team has used the Telegram Bot API from Telegram Messenger to send and receive commands to its Python backdoor. Sandworm Team also used legitimate M.E.Doc software update check requests for sending and receiving commands and hosted malicious payloads on putdrive.com. | cobertura: regra
Sandworm Team has pushed additional malicious tools onto an infected system to steal user credentials, move laterally, and destroy data. | cobertura: regra

Sandworm Team uses Prestige to disable and restore file system redirection by using the following functions: `Wow64DisableWow64FsRedirection()` and `Wow64RevertWow64FsRedirection()`. | cobertura: regra
Sandworm Team's BCS-server tool uses base64 encoding and HTML tags for the communication traffic between the C2 server. | cobertura: regra

Sandworm Team has used Dropbear SSH with a hardcoded backdoor password to maintain persistence within the target network. Sandworm Team has also used VPN tunnels established in legitimate software company infrastructure to gain access to internal networks of that software company's users. | cobertura: regra

Sandworm Team's VBS backdoor can decode Base64-encoded data and save it to the %TEMP% folder. The group also decrypted received information using the Triple DES algorithm and decompresses it using GZip. | cobertura: regra
Sandworm Team exploits public-facing applications for initial access and to acquire infrastructure, such as exploitation of the EXIM mail transfer agent in Linux systems. | cobertura: regra
Sandworm Team staged compromised versions of legitimate software installers on forums to achieve initial, untargetetd access in victim environments. | cobertura: regra
Sandworm Team has distributed NotPetya by compromising the legitimate Ukrainian accounting software M.E.Doc and replacing a legitimate software update with a malicious one. | cobertura: regra

Sandworm Team has used dedicated network connections from one victim organization to gain unauthorized access to a separate organization. Additionally, Sandworm Team has accessed Internet service providers and telecommunication entities that provide mobile connectivity. | cobertura: regra
Sandworm Team has exploited vulnerabilities in Microsoft PowerPoint via OLE objects (CVE-2014-4114) and Microsoft Word via crafted TIFF images (CVE-2013-3906). | cobertura: regra
Sandworm Team has tricked unwitting recipients into clicking on malicious hyperlinks within emails crafted to resemble trustworthy senders. | cobertura: regra
Sandworm Team has tricked unwitting recipients into clicking on spearphishing attachments and enabling malicious macros embedded within files. | cobertura: regra
Sandworm Team exfiltrates data of interest from enterprise databases using Adminer. | cobertura: regra
Sandworm Team used a backdoor which could execute a supplied DLL using rundll32.exe. | cobertura: regra
Sandworm Team has used remote administration tools or remote industrial control system client software for execution and to maliciously release electricity breakers. | cobertura: regra

Sandworm Team has used CaddyWiper, SDelete, and the BlackEnergy KillDisk component to overwrite files on victim systems. Additionally, Sandworm Team has used the JUNKMAIL tool to overwrite files with null bytes. | cobertura: regra
Sandworm Team has used Prestige ransomware to encrypt data at targeted organizations in transportation and related logistics industries in Ukraine and Poland. | cobertura: regra
Sandworm Team attempts to stop the MSSQL Windows service to ensure successful encryption of locked files. | cobertura: regra

Sandworm Team uses Prestige to delete the backup catalog from the target system using: `C:\Windows\System32\wbadmin.exe delete catalog -quiet` and to delete volume shadow copies using: `C:\Windows\System32\vssadmin.exe delete shadows /all /quiet`. | cobertura: regra
Sandworm Team defaced approximately 15,000 websites belonging to Georgian government, non-government, and private sector organizations in 2019. | cobertura: lacuna

Sandworm Team temporarily disrupted service to Georgian government, non-government, and private sector websites after compromising a Georgian web hosting provider in 2019. | cobertura: parcial (ASR/D3FEND)
Sandworm Team has used webshells including P.A.S. Webshell to maintain access to victim networks. | cobertura: regra
Sandworm Team used information stealer malware to collect browser session cookies. | cobertura: regra
Sandworm Team's CredRaptor tool can collect saved passwords from various internet browsers. | cobertura: regra
Sandworm Team has used the BlackEnergy KillDisk component to corrupt the infected system's master boot record. | cobertura: regra
Sandworm Team has delivered malicious Microsoft Office and ZIP file attachments via spearphishing emails. | cobertura: regra
Sandworm Team has crafted phishing emails containing malicious hyperlinks. | cobertura: regra

Sandworm Team has used `move` to transfer files to a network share and has copied payloads--such as Prestige ransomware--to an Active Directory Domain Controller and distributed via the Default Domain Group Policy Object. Additionally, Sandworm Team has transferred an ISO file into the OT network to gain initial access. | cobertura: regra
Sandworm Team has used port 6789 to accept connections on the group's SSH server. | cobertura: regra
Sandworm Team used various third-party email campaign management services to deliver phishing emails. | cobertura: lacuna

Sandworm Team has registered domain names and created URLs that are often designed to mimic or spoof legitimate websites, such as email login pages, online file sharing and storage websites, and password reset pages, while also hosting these items on legitimate, compromised network infrastructure. | cobertura: lacuna
Sandworm Team has leased servers from resellers instead of leasing infrastructure directly from hosting companies to enable its operations. | cobertura: lacuna
Sandworm Team compromised legitimate Linux servers running the EXIM mail transfer agent for use in subsequent campaigns. | cobertura: regra
Sandworm Team has used a large-scale botnet to target Small Office/Home Office (SOHO) network devices. | cobertura: regra
Sandworm Team has established social media accounts to disseminate victim internal-only documents and other sensitive data. | cobertura: lacuna
Sandworm Team has created email accounts that mimic legitimate organizations for its spearphishing operations. | cobertura: lacuna
Sandworm Team creates credential capture webpages to compromise existing, legitimate social media accounts. | cobertura: regra
Sandworm Team has developed malware for its operations, including malicious mobile applications and destructive malware such as NotPetya and Olympic Destroyer. | cobertura: regra

Sandworm Team has acquired open-source tools for their operations, including Invoke-PSImage, which was used to establish an encrypted channel from a compromised host to Sandworm Team's C2 server in preparation for the 2018 Winter Olympics attack, as well as Impacket and RemoteExec, which were used in their 2022 Prestige operations. Additionally, Sandworm… | cobertura: regra

In 2017, Sandworm Team conducted technical research related to vulnerabilities associated with websites used by the Korean Sport and Olympic Committee, a Korean power company, and a Korean airport. | cobertura: regra
Sandworm Team has obtained valid emails addresses while conducting research against target organizations that were subsequently used in spearphishing campaigns. | cobertura: regra
Sandworm Team's research of potential victim organizations included the identification and collection of employee information. | cobertura: regra
Sandworm Team conducted technical reconnaissance of the Parliament of Georgia's official internet domain prior to its 2019 attack. | cobertura: regra

In preparation for its attack against the 2018 Winter Olympics, Sandworm Team conducted online research of partner organizations listed on an official PyeongChang Olympics partnership site. | cobertura: lacuna

Sandworm Team has researched software code to enable supply-chain operations, most notably for the 2017 NotPetya attack. Sandworm Team also collected a list of computers using specific software as part of its targeting efforts. | cobertura: lacuna

Sandworm Team researched Ukraine's unique legal entity identifier (called an "EDRPOU" number), including running queries on the EDRPOU website, in preparation for the NotPetya attack. Sandworm Team has also researched third-party websites to help it craft credible spearphishing emails. | cobertura: lacuna
Sandworm Team has conducted research against potential victim websites as part of its operational planning. | cobertura: lacuna
Sandworm Team has scanned network infrastructure for vulnerabilities as part of its operational planning. | cobertura: regra
Sandworm Team has crafted spearphishing emails with hyperlinks designed to trick unwitting recipients into revealing their account credentials. | cobertura: lacuna
Sandworm Team staged compromised versions of legitimate software installers in forums to enable initial access to executing user. | cobertura: regra
